title: Ang 595: Sorath begins
hookLine: Guru Nanak opens the raga of faith
tomorrow: how do you say sorry when your pride is still talking?

lines: A LOT FROM A LITTLE ENVELOPE.
cards: Seed packets promise a lot from a little paper envelope: a photo of ripe peppers, a date to plant, a number of days to wait. Then you push the seed into the soil and see nothing at all for a long time.
On ang 595, the first page of raga Sorath, Guru Nanak answers yesterday's question with a farm. The seed he plants in the field of the body is the Name.

teach.h: MIND THE PLOWMAN, BODY THE FIELD.
teach.b: Here's the hymn in paraphrase, piece by piece. Make your mind the plowman, good deeds the farming, honest effort the water, and your body the field.

Let the Name be the seed, contentment the plank that levels the soil, and humility your clothes. Then, with the work of love, it will sprout, and you'll see how blessed that home becomes. Notice how physical it is.

Every part of the picture is something a farmer's hands know: the plow, the water, the leveling plank, the rough work clothes. Nothing in it is abstract except the seed, and even the seed is pushed into real ground.
And notice where faith sits. Not in watching the seed. A farmer who digs it up every morning to check kills it.
Faith, in this hymn, looks like the work done and then the waiting, trusting that love's work will make it sprout. And a small surprise: in this hymn, humility isn't a feeling.
It's clothing, the plain clothes you farm in. Contentment, too, is a tool: the plank that smooths the ground so the seed can take. That's how Sorath begins: with soil under the nails.

how: Sikhs read this Sorath hymn of Guru Nanak in the Guru Granth Sahib; its farming picture is often recited in kirtan and katha, where the Name is spoken of as a seed sown in the body.

games.q: Guru Nanak's farm — tap the pairs.

s: in this hymn, faith means watching closely until the seed sprouts
the work is done, then love's work makes it sprout. digging up the seed to check would kill it.
Guru Nanak pictures humility as clothing
contentment levels the soil, and humility is what you wear to farm.
the hymn treats the body as something in the way of the soul
the body is the field the Name is sown in.

games.q: you've started something slow: a habit, a language, a friendship after a fight. nothing's changed after a week. what fits Guru Nanak's farm?
o: keep doing the work and let it grow out of sight.
dig it up and check; if nothing's grown, start over.
stop working and just wait; effort shows you lack faith.
games.why: the hymn has both: honest effort is the water, and then love's work makes the seed sprout. faith is the work plus the waiting.

practice: Find something from the earth: a pinch of soil from a plant pot, a dry bean, a grain of rice, a seed from your kitchen. Hold it in your palm and feel its weight, its grit or smoothness, and smell it if you can.
Keep it there for the sit, and let it stay unopened, the way a seed waits in the ground.

wordCard.voice: Ang 595. Where raga Sorath begins: Guru Nanak's farmer, plowing with the mind and sowing the Name in the field of the body.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: haali, the plowman; 'man haali', the mind as the plowman, ang 595.

carryVoice: Keep this: faith, the seed you water and then don't dig up to check. Day fifteen-sixteen, planted.
